hints.content:
The function $f$ is negative $($i.e. $f(x)<0)$ whenever its graph is below the $x$-axis.

This is because the negative $y$-values are below the $x$-axis, and $y=f(x)$.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x-axis scales by one, and the y-axis scales by four. The graph of the function y equals f of x is below the x-axis from x equals negative five to x equals negative two. It is above the x-axis from x equals negative two to x equals zero. It is below the x-axis after x equals zero. The function increases from x equals negative five to x equals negative one. It decreases after x equals negative one. The function is highlighted from x equals negative five to x equals negative two and after x equals zero.

hints.content: Out of our options, the only correct interval is $0<x<1$.
